candidates.why: bit_chain_alloc at bits.c:3015 reallocs (frees) dat->chain. In decode.c:4567 str_dat->chain is advanced by str_dat->byte, making it a non-base interior pointer into the same buffer; any later bit_write_* on the parent dat that triggers bit_chain_alloc (bits.c:350/356) frees that buffer, leaving str_dat->chain dangling. Also str_dat->size is set to 0 at decode.c:4571, so a subsequent write on str_dat would realloc/free an interior pointer.

bit_reset_chain at bits.c:108 does dat->chain += pos, turning dat->chain into an interior pointer that is no longer the malloc base. bit_chain_alloc (bits.c:3015) then calls realloc on that interior pointer, and bit_chain_free (bits.c:3032) calls free on it — both invalid. Callers such as decode.c:5537 and decode_r2007.c:1357 invoke bit_reset_chain and later write/free the chain.

dwg_section_page_checksum caches data = &dat->chain[dat->byte] and end = dat->chain + dat->size (decode.c:1909-1910) and dereferences them in the loop at decode.c:1919. If any bit_write_* on the same dat reallocs dat->chain (bits.c:3015) between capture and use, these cached pointers dangle.

In bit_write_RC the while loops at bits.c:349 and 355 call bit_chain_alloc, which reallocs dat->chain (bits.c:3015). The reads at 357/360 and writes at 359/362 use dat->chain freshly so are safe here, but this is the free site that invalidates any caller-held alias (e.g. decode.c:4567, decode.c:1909) — reported as the free anchor for the cross-function cases.

section_string_stream does *str = *dat at decode_r2007.c:1395, so str->chain aliases dat->chain. If dat->chain is later realloc'd by bit_chain_alloc (bits.c:3015), str->chain becomes a dangling alias used by subsequent bit_read_* on str.
